baseline.source: engine: common/scripted_effects/00_political_setup.txt:68-79 (effect_starting_politics_traditional activates law_chiefdom for decentralized countries; common/laws/00_governance_principles.txt:12-25: law_theocracy cannot be enacted by one) and vanilla common/history/countries/pat - patagonia.txt (a decentralized start country takes effect_native_conscription_10); canon: WFB 8e Lizardmen army book (the wild Lizardmen holdings keep a Saurus warrior caste, Skink priests and no schooling beyond temple lore)
baseline.why: This package is used only by the decentralized Lizardmen holdings LZA-LZE. A decentralized country has no politics beyond the engine's: Chiefdom, no schools, and a native-conscription level in place of a military law; the other laws follow the temple-city package. The living and ruined temple-cities take the temple_city and ruined_temple_city profiles instead.

ruling_igs.why: Skeggi is a trading and raiding foothold, not a landed jarldom: its armed Jakkers and its traders rule, where the Norse package puts landowners.

laws.lawgroup_governance_principles.source: canon: WFB 8e Skaven army book (Clan Pestilens is a plague cult led by its Plague Priests and Plague Furnace)
laws.lawgroup_governance_principles.why: Pestilens is a cult-clan, ruled by its priests rather than a warlord's monarchy; the armed forces and devout already rule in the profile.

VCO.note: Luthor Harkon's Vampire Coast: vampire_lord package unchanged. Harkon captured the Dreadfleet's flagship in 2471 IC (8e) and is active by 2524; his rule at 2502 is inferred, hence medium.

laws.lawgroup_governance_principles.why: The Amazons are a priestess-led warrior society rather than a Glade Lord's monarchy.

ruling_igs.why: Priestesses and warriors rule; the wood elf package's Glade Kin are elven folk the Amazons do not have.

suggested_ig_names.why: Setting names for the two ruling groups; note only, no loc is authored from it.

TLC.note: Tilean colony Nuevo Luccini: lustrian_colony package (a captain-ruled pirate port).

BRC.note: invented Bretonnian colony: crusader_holding package with a colonial-affairs law.

laws.lawgroup_colonization.source: inferred (Chris, 2026-11-06, #10185: Lustrian colonies must be able to colonize)
laws.lawgroup_colonization.why: law_frontier_colonization is the colonial-affairs law that lets a colony colonize the neighbouring decentralized holdings; law_no_colonial_affairs blocks it.

taxed_goods.why: The profile taxes coffee, but the colony has no coffee plantation; its subsistence farm and maize land produce grain, so grain is taxed.
